candidates.rationale: Biallelic inactivation by mutation, deletion or methylation occurs in about 80-90% of ccRCC and is the founding event; loss drives HIF stabilization and defines the pathway that belzutifan targets.

HIF-2α is the key oncogenic driver downstream of VHL loss, and belzutifan (a HIF-2α inhibitor) produced about 49% objective response in VHL-disease RCC and about 22-25% in pretreated sporadic ccRCC (LITESPARK-005, which improved PFS over everolimus).

HIF-driven VEGF overexpression underlies the angiogenic phenotype, and VEGFR TKIs (sunitinib, pazopanib, axitinib, cabozantinib, lenvatinib) are standard of care; an angiogenesis gene signature predicts sunitinib response in IMmotion150/151.
PD-1 blockade (nivolumab, pembrolizumab) with ipilimumab or TKIs raises overall survival in first-line advanced RCC (CheckMate 214, KEYNOTE-426, CheckMate 9ER, CLEAR).

PD-L1 expression is a target and an enriching but imperfect biomarker, because benefit from immune checkpoint inhibitors occurs regardless of PD-L1 status in most trials (CheckMate 214 favored PD-L1 ≥1% for ORR).

The second most frequently mutated gene (about 40%), its loss is linked to a lower angiogenesis signature and better response to VEGF TKIs, and it has conflicting associations with ICI response (Miao 2018 vs. Braun 2020).
Mutated in about 10-15% of ccRCC and mutually exclusive with PBRM1, its loss is a reproducible marker of aggressive disease and worse survival.
Mutated in about 10-15% of ccRCC, its loss causes loss of H3K36me3 and is associated with poor prognosis and relapse.
MET is targeted by cabozantinib, which improved PFS and OS versus everolimus in METEOR (median PFS 7.4 vs 3.8 months) and was also active in MET-driven papillary RCC.

mTOR inhibitors (everolimus, temsirolimus) are approved in later lines, and mTOR is activated through PI3K/AKT/MTOR pathway mutations (MTOR, PIK3CA, PTEN, TSC1/2 in about 10-15% of tumors), though with modest benefit (RECORD-1 PFS 4.9 months).
